external_entities.name: supplier
external_entities.description: A supplier that uploads compliance paperwork and signs in to the portal.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal
external_entities.notes: The text does not state where suppliers are located.

external_entities.name: category manager
external_entities.description: An internal category manager who reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.
external_entities.notes: The source refers to these actors in the plural as category managers.

external_entities.name: vendor
external_entities.description: The SaaS vendor that hosts the supplier portal and pushes nightly supplier data extracts.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The portal is a SaaS product. The vendor hosts it
external_entities.notes: The text does not state the vendor's physical or network location.

processes.name: supplier document portal
processes.description: A vendor-hosted SaaS portal through which suppliers upload compliance paperwork and category managers review and approve or reject it.
processes.notes: The vendor datasheet says the platform is secure by design, uses enterprise-grade encryption throughout, and that all access is fully authenticated and audited.

processes.name: supplier master service
processes.description: A service that loads the nightly supplier data extract from the landing bucket and writes records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: vendor platform
data_stores.description: The vendor-hosted platform where supplier compliance documents remain stored.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket in the organisation's cloud account that receives the nightly supplier data extract before the supplier master service picks it up.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_stores.notes: The runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_stores.name: supplier database
data_stores.description: The database in the organisation's cloud account into which the supplier master service writes supplier records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

data_flows.name: upload paperwork
data_flows.description: A supplier uploads compliance paperwork through the supplier document portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.
data_flows.data_description: Insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for supplier staff.

data_flows.name: review and approve
data_flows.description: A category manager reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it in the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.
data_flows.data_description: Uploaded compliance paperwork and its approval or rejection status.

data_flows.name: store paperwork
data_flows.description: The supplier document portal stores uploaded compliance paperwork in the vendor platform.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.
data_flows.data_description: Supplier compliance paperwork, including insurance certificates, food safety audits, and staff contact details.

data_flows.name: push extract
data_flows.description: The vendor pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: The source says the extract was said to be encrypted end to end, but the runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is. These are conflicting positive claims, so encryption in transit is unknown.

data_flows.name: load file
data_flows.description: The supplier master service loads the nightly file from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file

data_flows.name: write records
data_flows.description: The supplier master service writes supplier records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database
data_flows.data_description: Supplier records from the nightly extract.

trust_boundaries.name: vendor hosting
trust_boundaries.description: The hosting zone controlled by the SaaS vendor for the supplier portal and vendor platform.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The portal is a SaaS product. The vendor hosts it

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The compliance paperwork and supplier records are confidential because they include contact details for supplier staff and commercially sensitive compliance documents.
assumptions.basis: The vendor platform holds insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for supplier staff.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket contents are confidential because the nightly extract contains supplier data.
assumptions.basis: The landing bucket receives a nightly supplier data extract.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database contents are confidential because it holds supplier records originating from the supplier data extract.
assumptions.basis: The supplier master service writes supplier records into the supplier database.

assumptions.assumption: The cloud account is a privilege boundary because it is the organisation's named account containing the cloud-hosted bucket, service, and database.
assumptions.basis: The source places the bucket, service, and database together in 'our cloud account', which represents an account-level authority zone.
